title: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach for Ramp Metering Based on Traffic Video Data

method_nodes.source_quote: Vehicle locations from raw images are extracted to reconstruct visual representations in the DRL method
method_nodes.description: Extracts vehicle locations (xi, yi) from raw video frames and reforms them into position matrices of size 4x512 pixels after zooming and down-sampling.

method_nodes.source_quote: we stack the matrices of consecutive N time steps to represent the state st
method_nodes.description: Stacks three consecutive position matrices to represent the traffic state, capturing vehicle dynamics and signal states.

method_nodes.source_quote: consists of three convolutional neural network (CNN) layers and one full connection (FC) layer for each output layer.
method_nodes.description: Defines a deep Q-network with three CNN layers (filters: 32, 64, 64) and two parallel fully connected layers (256 units each) for multitask learning.

method_nodes.source_quote: The algorithm for training the ramp metering policy is presented in Algorithm 1.
method_nodes.description: Trains the agent using Deep Q-learning with experience replay and a target network to stabilize training, optimized via the Adam algorithm.

method_nodes.source_quote: the mean speed in the merging area and the queue length at the on-ramp are predicted simultaneously.
method_nodes.description: Implements multitask learning to predict mean speed and queue length simultaneously with the Q-value, using a combined loss function.

method_nodes.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator
method_nodes.description: Evaluates the trained policy in the SUMO microscopic traffic simulator using real-world traffic data from the Qingdao-Huangdao freeway.

method_nodes.source_quote: A perturbation analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of information contained in video data.
method_nodes.description: Performs perturbation analysis by dividing the control area into eight subareas and removing information from each to evaluate its impact on performance.

source_nodes.source_quote: A series of simulation experiments based on real-world traffic data are conducted to evaluate the proposed approach.
source_nodes.description: Traffic data from the freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao in Shandong, China, including mainline and on-ramp volumes used for simulation calibration.
source_nodes.reproducibility_rationale: Available from the corresponding author upon request.
